headline: The AI Pipeline That Applied to 700 Jobs and Won
lede: When a developer named Santiago Ferreira decided to job-hunt in tech, he built a system instead of updating his CV. The result, now open-sourced as *career-ops*, uses Anthropic's **Claude Code** as its reasoning core to scan career pages, score listings, rewrite CVs per role, and fill application forms automatically. By the creator's account — corroborated by the *Digit* writeup — the pipeline processed more than 700 applications and landed him a position.
body:
The architecture is more layered than a typical automation script. Fourteen named *skill modes* handle discrete steps: scanning company career pages for new postings, evaluating fit against a scoring rubric, generating *ATS-optimized* PDFs via Playwright (a browser-automation library originally built by Microsoft), and filling web-based application forms end-to-end. A terminal dashboard written in Go provides a live pipeline view; the screenshot in the tweet shows columns labeled — in Spanish, suggesting Ferreira is based in a Spanish-speaking country — *Evaluada* (evaluated), *Aplicado* (applied), *Entrevista* (interview), and *No Aplicar* (do not apply).

The scoring mechanism is the system's most consequential feature. Each listing receives a numerical rating before any human time is spent. Of the 516 roles visible in the screenshot, 219 were filtered out automatically, 66 were submitted, and 10 reached the interview stage — a funnel shape consistent with human job searches, achieved at a fraction of the effort. Top-rated roles include a Staff AI Engineer position at **Datadog** (scored 4.5), roles at Dialpad and Langfuse, and listings at OpenAI and LangChain.

The *ATS-optimized PDF* angle deserves scrutiny. Most large employers route applications through *applicant-tracking systems* — software that parses and ranks CVs before a human recruiter sees them, rewarding documents dense with keywords matching the job description. Ferreira's system attempts to game this layer programmatically: Claude rewrites the CV for each listing, surfacing relevant terms and restructuring sections to maximize the algorithmic score. The approach is increasingly common in AI-assisted hiring tools, but career-ops automates the full loop rather than offering a one-off rewrite.

The 45-plus pre-configured companies skew conspicuously toward the AI sector — Anthropic, OpenAI, ElevenLabs, Stripe, Datadog, LangChain, n8n among them. The tool's first audience is almost certainly AI engineers hunting AI roles, which adds a layer of irony: the same firms investing in AI hiring pipelines are now receiving applications generated by one. Whether their own screening systems can distinguish an AI-tailored CV from a hand-crafted one is a question the career-ops experiment implicitly poses.

The open-sourcing of the repo is likely to accelerate an arms race that recruiters are already bracing for. Automated mass application has existed for years in cruder forms, but *career-ops* integrates evaluation, personalization, and form-filling into a single agentic loop requiring minimal human intervention. As these tools proliferate, the signal value of a submitted application — already low — will erode further, putting more pressure on the interview stages that no current automation can fake.

concepts.definition: Software used by employers to receive, parse, and rank job applications before a human recruiter reviews them. ATS platforms score CVs based on keyword matches with the job description, which has spawned a cottage industry of optimization advice — and now, automated tools that rewrite CVs to score higher algorithmically.

An agentic coding assistant built by Anthropic that operates as a command-line tool. Unlike a simple chat interface, Claude Code can read and write files, execute shell commands, and chain multi-step tasks autonomously — making it a natural backbone for pipelines that need to browse pages, generate documents, and fill forms in sequence.

An open-source browser-automation library developed by Microsoft that lets programs control Chromium, Firefox, or WebKit browsers programmatically. It is widely used for UI testing and web scraping; career-ops uses it both to generate print-quality PDFs from HTML CVs and to interact with application forms that resist simple HTTP requests.

Discrete, named capability sets that a Claude Code agent can be invoked with, each bundling a specific prompt strategy, tool subset, and output format. In career-ops, skills map to pipeline stages — scanning, evaluating, generating PDFs — so the same underlying model behaves differently depending on which mode is called.

repos.summary: An AI-powered job search pipeline built on Claude Code, designed to automate the full application lifecycle. It scrapes 45-plus pre-configured company career pages, scores each listing against a user profile, rewrites the CV per role using Claude, generates ATS-optimized PDFs via Playwright, and can fill application forms automatically. A Go terminal dashboard provides a Kanban view of the pipeline across stages: evaluated, applied, interviewing, and rejected.

fact_check: The claim that career-ops 'got him a job' rests on the creator's own account, repeated by the *Digit* article without independent verification. The figure of 700-plus scored applications is plausible given the pipeline architecture and the 516-listing snapshot visible in the screenshot, but the exact total is not auditable from public sources. No other factual claims in the tweet appear incorrect; the feature list (14 skill modes, Go dashboard, Playwright PDF generation, 45-plus companies) is confirmed by the GitHub repository description.
